title: Nicola Walker in The Corn Is Green - review with photos
transcript: i'm paul seven lewis hello and welcome to one minute theater reviews this is the national theater and i'm here to see nicola walker in the corners green the corn is green is a production that's worthy to stand alongside the best in the history of the national theater it seems almost a bonus that it features a star performance from nicola walker it said 100 years ago and an english woman miss moffett arrives in a welsh miming village it's her mission to educate the children one of them morgan evans played with feeling and humor by ewan davis is exceptionally clever and becomes her protege much of the play hinges around the question will he or won't he go to oxford university the other characters are one-dimensional so anyone playing miss moffett is required to carry the show and the past the part has attracted some big guns sybil fondai cathol barrymore betty davis catherine hepburn deborah carr big shoes to step into and it seems for the first half that this is going to be a one note performance from nicola walker i mean a beautiful pure note but essentially she's a determined woman and haughty towards everyone she meets and in everything she does but then as she becomes more emotionally involved in making morgan a success a throatiness and slight hesitation invades the previous stridency it's a subtle powerful performance that's the one-minute review please keep watching for more about this production of the corners green and nicola walker's outstanding performance this autobiographical play is dated in some well in many respects and could have failed as a production but for some brilliant ideas by i assume the director dominic cook first he introduces the author emily williams played by gareth david lloyd onto the stage giving stage directions and in that sense showing he's both telling a story and that the story is very much about him and when morgan talks about the conflict he feels about leaving his community it's not dwelt on in the play but again dominic cook's production comes to the rescue by the use of a minus chorus throughout as a reminder of the draw of the community the play opens with a 1930s ball shown in silhouette behind a curtain a man steps out from it to the front of the stage and we soon realized this is emily williams and he begins to write his semi-autobiographical play on a typewriter and creates the characters and the story before our eyes we're back in a welsh mining village in the early 20s a group of miners sing in welsh the great bildema choreographs the moments of dance and we meet some of the characters the village children who only speak welsh and the english who stand above and apart from them showing contempt for the people they regard as savages the characters are amusing but fairly one-dimensional richard lynch is the saved christian mr jones who is welsh but subservient and with red-faced passion bubbling under his proper exterior the dim nervous miss rombery played by alice or ewing and the even dimmer landowner that she loves simply known as the squire and played by rufus wright then miss muffet appears she wants to educate the children which partly means teaching them to read and write english that is the play addresses this and other racist attitudes towards the welsh as a bit of a joke i'm afraid morgan starts as a cocky leader of the boys all the boys are played by adults by the way but uh we soon realize how clever he is and he becomes miss moffat's star student and she's tyrannical in her determination to pursue her ambitions for him without care of any enemies she might make but first the actor's mime on a set designed by alts that is blank and black with minimal props perhaps indicating the emptiness of the prospects of these people who start down the mines at age 10. now i don't want to spoil the surprise but the set design is gradually populated with more detail and when you come after the interval the curtain goes up on a transformation just as miss moffat has become emotionally engaged and prepared to compromise to get away morgan has become educated and committed to leaving for a wider world and so the set becomes a naturalistic room full of colorful wallpaper and detailed furnishings sure the corn is green is sentimental patronizing and not overly challenging but it's also heartwarming and a hymn to the power of education i give the corners green four stars i hope you enjoyed this review or at least found it useful if you did and you'd like to be the first to see my future reviews please subscribe if you'd
